title: Counital integral diagonal on the cubical lattice resolution
statement:
Let $r\geq0$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ its ordered standard basis. Use the integral cubical complex of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction]: $C_a$ is the free abelian group on $[v,I]$, with $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $a$, zero outside $0\leq a\leq r$, with
$$\partial[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]).$$
Its augmentation $\varepsilon:C_0\to\mathbf Z$ sends every vertex to $1$. Give the tensor chain complex $C\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$ differential $\partial(x\otimes y)=\partial x\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes\partial y$ for $x\in C_a$, and give it the diagonal translation action. Put $u_A=\sum_{i\in A}u_i$ and $\epsilon(A,C)=(-1)^{\#\{(a,c)\in A\times C:c<a\}}$. The finite formulas
$$\Delta[v,I]=\sum_{A\sqcup C=I}\epsilon(A,C)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,C]$$
define a translation-equivariant chain map $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$. Under the canonical unit identifications,
$$(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=1=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta,\qquad (\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\varepsilon.$$
The last equality is an equality of augmented chain maps to $\mathbf Z[0]$. For $r=0$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$.

proof.text: Use the differential and augmentation of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], including $\partial^2=0$ and $\varepsilon\partial_1=0$. Write $(C\otimes C)_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}C_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C_b$. The tensor differential is well-defined by bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For homogeneous $x\in C_a,y\in C_b$ its square is $\partial^2x\otimes y+((-1)^{a-1}+(-1)^a)\partial x\otimes\partial y+x\otimes\partial^2y=0$; when $a=0$ the middle term is zero directly. Thus this is a chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. The displayed formula for $\Delta[v,I]$ has $2^{|I|}$ terms, all of total degree $|I|$, and therefore extends uniquely to a degree-preserving homomorphism by the basis property [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Set it to zero on zero source degrees. No contraction, exactness or comparison of resolutions is needed.

proof.text: For a fixed $i\in I$ and a disjoint partition $B\sqcup C=I\setminus\{i\}$, put $p=\#\{b\in B:b<i\}$, $q=\#\{c\in C:c<i\}$, $t=\#\{b\in B:i<b\}$ and $N=\#\{(b,c)\in B\times C:c<b\}$. Then $|B|=p+t$ and the position of $i$ in $I$ is $p+q$. In $\partial\Delta[v,I]$, removing $i$ from the first factor of the partition $(B\cup\{i\},C)$ gives sign $(-1)^{N+q+p}$. Removing $i$ from the second factor of the partition $(B,C\cup\{i\})$ gives sign $(-1)^{N+t+|B|+q}=(-1)^{N+p+q}$, including the tensor differential sign $(-1)^{|B|}$. These formulas follow by counting the extra inversion pairs involving $i$: there are $q$ in the first partition and $t$ in the second. Denote their common sign by $s=(-1)^{p+q}\epsilon(B,C)$.

proof.text: For the fixed $(i,B,C)$ of step 2, the two first-factor faces contribute $$s\bigl([v+u_i,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]-[v,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]\bigr),$$ and the two second-factor faces contribute $$s\bigl([v,B]\otimes[v+u_B+u_i,C]-[v,B]\otimes[v+u_B,C]\bigr).$$ The middle terms cancel. Every term of $\partial\Delta[v,I]$ belongs to exactly one such triple: its removed direction specifies $i$ and its surviving direction sets specify $B,C$. On the other hand the $(B,C)$ term of $\Delta\bigl((-1)^{p+q}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}])\bigr)$ is precisely the two surviving terms. Summing over $i,B,C$ proves $\partial\Delta=\Delta\partial$ on each basis vector. For $I=\varnothing$ both sides are zero. Equality on a basis gives equality everywhere; zero source degrees also give zero on both sides. This is the chain-map condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: Let $\tau_w[v,I]=[v+w,I]$. In each summand of $\Delta\tau_w[v,I]$ the two bases are $v+w$ and $v+w+u_A$; in $(\tau_w\otimes\tau_w)\Delta[v,I]$ they are $v+w$ and $(v+u_A)+w$. They agree by addition in $\mathbf Z^r$, with the same direction sets and sign. Thus the two homomorphisms agree on every generator and $\Delta$ is equivariant for diagonal translation.

proof.text: Extend $\varepsilon$ by zero in positive degrees to a map $C\to\mathbf Z[0]$; it is a chain map because $\varepsilon\partial_1=0$ by [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], and every other target differential or component is zero. In $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta[v,I]$ only $A=\varnothing$ survives, with sign $1$, and its value is $1\otimes[v,I]$. In $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta[v,I]$ only $C=\varnothing$ survives, with sign $1$, and its value is $[v,I]\otimes1$. The unit identifications send these to $[v,I]$: explicitly $\mathbf Z\otimes M\to M$, $n\otimes x\mapsto nx$, has inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and likewise on the right; the composites are identities by bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. These tensor maps commute with differentials by the displayed tensor differential and $\varepsilon\partial_1=0$. This proves both counit identities as equalities of chain maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image, algebraic input below the tame-boundary route. The following finite signed-sum verification is agent-written; the blueprint does not assert or prove this cubical diagonal formula.

proof.text: For $|I|>0$ every partition has a nonempty part, so $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta[v,I]=0=\varepsilon[v,I]$. For $I=\varnothing$ there is one summand, and its image is $1\otimes1$, identified with $1$. Hence the double augmentation equals $\varepsilon$ in every degree and, by step 5 and the chain-map identity, as a chain map to $\mathbf Z[0]$. When $r=0$ there is just the vertex $[0,\varnothing]$, identified with $1\in\mathbf Z$, and the sole partition is empty in both parts. The formula is therefore $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$; there are no positive source degrees.
